_comment_family: The light end of the family, and fitness-story's block face. See
hanken-grotesk-extrabolditalic.json, which is the cut that channel
picks its words out in and carries the note on what this typeface
used to be called.
The full name (ID 4) is declared for the reason every Hanken pack
here declares it: ID 1 on this file is 'Hanken Grotesk ExtraLight',
which names a WEIGHT and not a cut, so the upright ExtraLight would
answer to it — and on a design that leans throughout, a block that
came back upright would not read as a variation, it would read as a
mistake.
Weight 250, which is what the file's OS/2 table says. It is not one
of the round hundreds, and it is stated as found rather than rounded
to 200: the number is handed to the FontFace descriptor and to the
canvas font string, and a value that disagrees with the file is how
a browser is invited to synthesise a weight nobody drew. CSS has
accepted arbitrary numbers in 1-1000 since Fonts 4, so 250 is a
legal weight and not a trick.
Registered at style normal, the same way rift and the other Hanken
packs are. The slant is drawn into the letterforms; declaring the
face italic as well would leave the canvas — which asks for normal —
either missing it or being handed a synthetic oblique of something
else.
_comment_css: Not declared in styles.css: this face arrived with a channel and is
registered from this JSON, which is the route content/README.md
describes. Nothing has to be added to the stylesheet for it.

_comment_stack: The fallbacks are damage limitation and never a design choice — a
title laid out against the wrong metrics is broken, not merely
different, which is what fontguard exists to catch before it is ever
drawn. Segoe UI Light for the reason telegraf-ultralight names it:
putting a 250-weight hairline behind Impact would make the one thing
that survives a missing file the furthest possible thing from it, and
Segoe UI Light is the nearest weight the machine can be relied on to
